claims.claim: The current repository commercial decision remains STOP and the product pilot remains not approved.
limitations: Internal gate, not an external market verdict
claims.decision_effect: No customer pilot, paid offer or positive venture verdict can be claimed from research alone.
claims.falsifier: New retained evidence directly closes technical, comparative, operational, demand and claim-integrity gates.

claims.claim: The frozen local product detected 0 of 40 constructed positives in each of Candidate A and B while transparent baselines detected 40 of 40.
claims.decision_effect: Regula cannot be sold on technical superiority; the named buyer job must be re-evaluated against a baseline before any pilot.
claims.falsifier: A preregistered representative independently labelled evaluation demonstrates non-inferior recall and lower review burden on the exact buyer job.

claims.claim: There are no independently human-labelled real-repository efficacy results in the controlling commercial evidence.
limitations: Repository evidence cannot prove no private research exists
claims.decision_effect: Technical fit remains failed or untested outside the constructed jobs.
claims.falsifier: A retained independent label set and version-bound results are produced.

claims.claim: Third-party AI evaluation is a material workflow in UK financial services.
limitations: Does not measure supplier preparation pain or payment
claims.decision_effect: A real workflow exists, so a narrow discovery programme is justified.
claims.falsifier: Representative buyers show third-party AI receives no distinct or material review.

claims.claim: No retained repository, primary, review or forum evidence in this research establishes a budget or willingness to pay for Regula's proposed supplier evidence-readiness service.
limitations: Adjacent products show category spend but not Regula demand
claims.decision_effect: WILLINGNESS_TO_PAY remains UNVALIDATED; economics are assumptions only.
claims.falsifier: A qualified buyer or supplier signs a paid bounded engagement after seeing limitations.

claims.claim: Supplier due diligence involves repeated questionnaires and evidence reuse across heterogeneous formats.
limitations: Not specific to insurers or AI
Standard attestations can reduce custom work
claims.decision_effect: Traceability, freshness and bounded reuse deserve testing; generic answer generation does not differentiate.
claims.falsifier: Target suppliers and insurers show no repeated evidence or rely adequately on standard attestations.

claims.claim: The PRA supervised 568 insurers of all types at January 2026.
claims.decision_effect: Do not present a validated market size; discovery must identify the actual beachhead denominator.
claims.falsifier: PRA corrects the count or a different date/scope is used.

claims.claim: The 2024 UK AI sector study identified 5,862 firms and classified 95 percent as SMEs.
claims.decision_effect: Use only as an upper-bound input, never Regula TAM or revenue.
claims.falsifier: A corrected official study changes the population.

claims.claim: UK government research reports an existing AI assurance market while identifying weak demand understanding, model-access constraints and interoperability fragmentation.
limitations: Does not validate Regula or its beachhead
claims.decision_effect: Interoperability is a plausible problem but crowded; service-first learning is safer than platform investment.
claims.falsifier: Target buyers show terminology/interoperability has no effect on decisions or incumbents solve it fully.

claims.claim: The evidence-readiness workflow is served by AI-governance platforms, model-risk tools, GRC, trust centres, questionnaire automation, standards tools and professional services.
applicable_versions: dated pages where available; live vendor pages otherwise
limitations: Exact cut-off state unresolved for undated live pages
claims.decision_effect: Generic governance, evidence and questionnaire features are parity; differentiation remains not demonstrated.
claims.falsifier: Product exercise or buyer research reveals a material unserved job incumbents cannot address.

claims.claim: Conveyor publicly listed a Business plan starting at 9,600 US dollars per year for questionnaire and RFP workflow.
applicable_versions: live pricing page; exact cut-off snapshot unresolved
limitations: No evidence Regula can command similar price
claims.decision_effect: Use only as an adjacent price anchor, not a Regula forecast.
claims.falsifier: Archived cut-off page or vendor contract contradicts the price.

claims.claim: Local processing may reduce confidentiality friction but is not durable differentiation by itself.
contrary_sources: Customer-managed and on-prem deployments are already available from some incumbents
limitations: No target buyer data-boundary refusal measured
claims.decision_effect: Retain local-first boundary, but do not call it a moat; test refusal and disclosure needs first.
claims.falsifier: Buyers show local extraction materially changes adoption and incumbents cannot match it.

claims.claim: CycloneDX, SPDX, in-toto, SLSA, Sigstore, OSCAL and PROV-O document mechanisms for component description, provenance, integrity or control information.
limitations: Implementation without buyer consumption creates no value
claims.decision_effect: REASONED application: use at most one demanded export and a small internal schema. No observed buyer adoption advantage supports treating standards coverage as defensibility.
claims.falsifier: A named buyer requires and consumes a specific format and measures lower review cost.

claims.claim: A lightweight claim-evidence-counterevidence model fits Regula's bounded role better than a compliance score.
contrary_sources: Buyer familiarity outside safety domains is unverified
limitations: Structure does not make evidence true
claims.decision_effect: Test a simple internal graph during service delivery; do not implement full SACM yet.
claims.falsifier: Reviewers prefer existing documents and the structure adds time without changing decisions.

claims.claim: Version-bound evidence with explicit expiry and change-triggered reopening is the highest-ranked internal technical hypothesis in this analysis, supported by weak target-market evidence.
contrary_sources: Existing GRC and trust platforms document continuous evidence workflows
claims.decision_effect: Test five invalidation triggers manually across repeated engagements before building software.
claims.falsifier: Buyers do not revisit evidence, existing platforms suffice, or reopening creates more burden than value.

claims.claim: Article 50 transparency obligations applied from 2 August 2026 and official guidelines and a voluntary code existed by the cut-off.
claims.decision_effect: Article 50 is a timely candidate but not the selected beachhead without buyer evidence.
claims.falsifier: Official legal changes alter scope/timing or target users show no implementation need.

claims.claim: Agent security, identity and authorization remain active standards-development areas. Regula has no demonstrated advantage in them because no buyer job, implementation or comparison has been validated.
limitations: NIST initiative is research/coordination, not certification
claims.decision_effect: Do not pivot to agent governance; retain as a long-term option only.
claims.falsifier: Target interviews reveal an urgent budgeted audit-evidence gap and a cheap Regula test outperforms incumbents.

claims.claim: Confidential computing, MPC, federated evaluation, zero-knowledge proofs and differential privacy are premature for the current hypothesis.
limitations: No threat model or refusal evidence
claims.decision_effect: Defer implementation; first ask whether local execution and controlled disclosure are insufficient.
claims.falsifier: Multiple paying counterparties require remote confidential evaluation and reject cheaper boundaries.

claims.claim: A manual buyer-specific study is a more capital-efficient research method than building a platform now; this does not establish a productised service or commercial model.
contrary_sources: Expert labour and liability may never become software
Current product pilot remains not approved
claims.decision_effect: Keep the venture at STOP. Permit only owner-gated discovery and manual baseline research before any paid offer or assisted delivery.
claims.falsifier: Buyers refuse service, delivery cannot be standardised, or a cheaper incumbent is adequate.

claims.claim: Regula has no demonstrated durable commercial moat at the cut-off.
contrary_sources: Prospective accepted/rejected evidence data and reviewer networks could compound
claims.decision_effect: Do not use code, mappings, signing, standards or local processing as moat claims.
claims.falsifier: Lawfully reusable decision data, independent labels, buyer acceptance or distribution becomes demonstrably hard to replicate.

claims.claim: Innovator Founder rules require a significant contribution to the plan, day-to-day role, instrumental founder status and an endorsed innovative, viable and scalable venture.
limitations: Application of rules to facts requires professional advice
This research is not an endorsement assessment
claims.decision_effect: Founder evidence must arise from real prospective work and authority; visa criteria do not drive the venture decision.
claims.falsifier: Official rules or guidance change.

claims.claim: Collaborator could genuinely lead customer research, proposition, service design, operating model, partnerships, economics, governance and day-to-day commercial operations from the point she starts doing the work.
contrary_sources: No work outputs or decision record yet supplied
Skills gaps and working permissions require assessment
limitations: Capability and commitment not independently assessed
Token involvement risk if authority is nominal
claims.decision_effect: Define real outputs and decision rights; do not backdate or infer eligibility.
claims.falsifier: She does not perform or control the proposed work, or professional advice identifies a legal barrier.

claims.claim: A standalone scalable Regula venture is not demonstrated.
contrary_sources: A real third-party assurance workflow exists
Evidence freshness and local disclosure remain testable hypotheses
limitations: No authorised human or paid validation could occur in this unit
claims.decision_effect: Select STOP for the venture, product and pilot; permit only owner-gated discovery and reject platform construction.
claims.falsifier: Repeated paid engagements show buyer acceptance, lawful evidence reuse, declining human effort, positive margins and defensible distribution.
